# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

**Qi2** is the open wireless charging standard from the Wireless Power Consortium (WPC). It added a magnetic ring that aligns the phone and charger, and it charges at up to 15W. The magnet design draws on Apple's MagSafe technology ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**Qi2.2** (formally Qi v2.2.1, branded "Qi2 25W") is the newer revision of Qi2. It raises the cap to 25W, nearly 70% more power than Qi2, and the WPC says it can charge a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). The first certified products appeared in July 2025.

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding and certification program, not a separate standard. Apple's MagSafe Charger is certified for Qi2 25W and regular Qi, so it works with Qi2 phones and older Qi devices ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)). Per [Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html), MagSafe-certified chargers also include:
- An NFC antenna that lets the iPhone identify the charger.
- A magnetometer that prevents compass interference while charging.

## Practical differences

| | Qi2 | Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W) | MagSafe |
|---|---|---|---|
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | Up to 25W on newer iPhones, 15W on most others |
| Who certifies | WPC | WPC | Apple |
| Magnets | Yes | Yes | Yes |

- **Speed depends on your phone.** According to Apple's support page, the 25W speed applies to iPhone 17 models and newer, plus the iPhone 16 Plus and 16 Pro Max. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro reach 22.5W, and the iPhone Air reaches 20W. The iPhone 15 and earlier top out at 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **Android support is limited.** The Pixel 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at up to 25W. Other Pixel 10 models support Qi2 at 15W, and Samsung's Galaxy lineup is "Qi2 Ready" and needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).
- **"MagSafe-compatible" is not the same as certified.** Uncertified chargers with a magnet ring are usually limited to 7.5W ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Look for the Qi2 or Qi2 25W logo, or search the [WPC product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).

## If you want one charger

For an iPhone, the [Apple MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m) (Qi2 25W certified) is the simplest choice. Apple lists the 2 m version at $49. For 25W you need a 30W or higher USB-C power adapter, which is sold separately. Third-party Qi2.2 chargers from Belkin, Anker, Ugreen, and others also work at 25W with the same phones.
